A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TransVLM research work, with 29 readable pages including Appendix A.1–A.6. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that pages 2–29 are identical; differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: Section 6 and Tables 3–4 report original benchmark evaluations and ablation experiments, supplemented by qualitative analyses and performance curves in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, qualitative analyses, and appendix performance curves reported in v1.

M1.justification: The optical-flow/color fusion, zero-padding initialization, data synthesis, quality-aware sampling, and sliding-window inference with NMS remain identical in Section 4 and Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same public, internal, and synthetic training data and the same 5,215-video STD benchmark. No datasets, domains, tasks, or transition scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 and Appendix A.5 retain the same PySceneDetect variants, TransNetV2, AutoShot, Gemini models, and Qwen3-VL Instruct and Thinking configurations in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, model configurations, training settings, inference windows, metrics, and temporal-tolerance evaluation procedures are unchanged in Sections 5–6 and Appendices A.2–A.3.

E4.justification: Table 4 and Appendix A.6 retain identical training, data-composition, optical-flow, fusion, and initialization ablations. The visual-token analyses and annotation-error case studies in Figures 4–7 are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain the same averaging over temporal tolerances, which is distinct from run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted curves, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains TransVLM's public segment/frame F1 scores of 0.783/0.568 and synthetic scores of 0.895/0.938.

T1.justification: The STD segment formulation in Section 3, fusion and initialization equations in Section 4, and metric definitions in Appendix A.2.1 are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same task, method, data-engine, benchmark, and performance claims. The deleted first-page production-deployment statement is ancillary to these core contributions.

C2.justification: The explanations of motion sensitivity, domain gaps, annotation limitations, and efficiency tradeoffs remain identical. Section 6.2 also retains its interpretation of real-world deployment viability.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data-processing instructions, and training/inference configurations remain unchanged. The project-page and resource links retain the same destinations.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography, and the positioning relative to SBD methods and general-purpose VLMs are identical. No cited works or novelty arguments are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 deletes the first-page footnote sentence 'This work has been deployed to production.' The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; all other prose, terminology, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page footnote becomes shorter, and the marginal arXiv version/date display changes. All figures, tables, captions, and the rendered layout of pages 2–29 are identical.

improvement.justification: Removing the brief production-deployment assertion and updating the version stamp do not materially alter the paper's quality. The methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, appendices, and reproducibility information are unchanged.
